reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Few companies and countries deciding AI
themes.definition: Concern that a small group of companies and countries could take all decisions about AI while others look on.
themes.inclusion: Include passages objecting to concentration of AI decision-making among a few firms or states.
themes.exclusion: Exclude access-gap framings without a power/decision element (AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE).
themes.boundary_cases: When the proposed remedy is deciding within the UN, also code AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: Do we let a small group of companies and countries take all the decisions while the rest of us simply look on?

themes.label: UN as forum for collective AI decisions
themes.definition: The United Nations is presented as the setting in which states should jointly decide the future of AI.
themes.inclusion: Include statements that AI decisions should be made within the UN or UN processes.
themes.exclusion: Exclude using AI to reform UN operations (AI_UN_EFFICIENCY).
themes.boundary_cases: General multilateral governance calls without naming the UN go to AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: do we decide together, within the logical setting of the United Nations, what our future should look like?

themes.label: Using AI to improve multilateral institutions
themes.definition: AI presented as a tool to boost the efficiency and effectiveness of the UN and multilateral institutions as part of reform efforts like UN80.
themes.inclusion: Include passages proposing the use of AI within the UN system or multilateral institutions to improve operations.
themes.exclusion: Exclude governance of AI by the UN (AI_UN_ROLE).
themes.boundary_cases: Generic 'use technology in UN reform' without AI is not coded.

examples.quote: we must work together by using AI and other technologies wherever possible
explore new ways of boosting the efficiency and effectiveness of multilateral institutions

value.rationale: Both Netherlands passages tie AI to the future of the UN, but differently: 2026 frames AI as a power-concentration choice to be settled collectively at the UN, while 2025 treats AI as a tool for making multilateral institutions more efficient under UN80.
